references.text: Describes the ritual where sins are placed on the scapegoat that carries the people's iniquities away to a desolate land, as part of the Day of Atonement.
Repeats the commandment regarding the Day of Atonement and its function as a day for atonement before the Lord.
Aaron shall make atonement on the altar once a year with the blood of the sin offering, which points forward to the annual Day of Atonement.
Detailed instructions for the offerings on the Day of Atonement to make atonement for the people.
David's prayer for cleansing from sin and that God would wash him clean, reflecting the need for spiritual purification.
The prayer to be cleansed with hyssop and washed whiter than snow, which connects to the rituals of purification.
The Lord's promise that even if sins are like scarlet, they shall become white as snow—complete cleansing.
God's promise to sprinkle clean water on the people and cleanse them from all impurity and all idols.
God will cleanse the people from all their iniquities on the day He restores them.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place once a year with blood to make atonement for the people's sins, which is fulfilled in Christ.
Christ's blood cleanses the conscience from dead works, far better than the blood of goats and bulls.
The annual offerings could not make the worshippers perfect, but Christ's sacrifice takes away sins once for all.
Jesus' blood cleanses us from all sin, and if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
